## Havana — capital of the Island of Freedom!

The capital of the Island of Freedom is a vibrant and captivating city, one of the most unusual in the world. Its distinctive atmosphere and wealth of sights draw visitors and invite them to explore the fascinating world of Cuba's capital. Architecture dating from Spanish colonial rule stands alongside ultra-modern concrete-and-glass skyscrapers. The city is extremely picturesque: the center of Old Havana, with its narrow colonial-era streets, has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Prado Boulevard and the Malecón waterfront are traditional places for a stroll.

Havana hosts colorful carnivals. On the Prado stands the National Capitol building, whose architecture resembles that of the United States Capitol. Here you will also see the memorial to the Granma, the yacht whose voyage marked the beginning of the Cuban Revolution in 1956 under Fidel Castro. On Plaza de la Catedral stands the cathedral, built in the 17th century. The Ernest Hemingway House Museum is also located here.

## What Havana offers travelers!

Morro and La Punta fortresses defended the city against pirate attacks from the sea, while La Fuerza Castle is the oldest fort in the Americas. Numerous beaches suitable for diving and deep-sea fishing, excellent yacht clubs and a large amusement park all create an atmosphere of relaxation and celebration. In Havana, you can take lessons in famous Cuban salsa and discover the city's nightlife, visiting nightclubs and discos filled with lively Cuban music. At the factory producing the renowned Partagás cigars, you will learn how they are made. Havana is Cuba's best shopping destination, with many shops, several shopping centers, open-air markets and hundreds of small stores at hotels and other tourist spots. The capital of the Island of Freedom promises an unforgettable holiday!

General Arenales is a town and municipality of the same name in Buenos Aires Province. A business trip here takes you beyond metropolitan Argentina, into the fields, farms and practical work of the agricultural sector.

For a professional group, the surrounding countryside offers opportunities to discuss sowing techniques, harvesting and production management directly with local specialists. We include General Arenales as part of an itinerary through the agricultural Pampas, arranging the farms visited and the agenda for each meeting in advance. This format is particularly useful when the aim is to compare theory with decisions made in the field.
